1.note:
# General Information:

Throughout chapter 23, Joash is referred to as “the king.” It may be helpful to your readers to occasionally add “King Joash” or “Joash the king” to make his identity explicit.
the chief priest who served in the temple and was faithful to God. He was an advisor to Joash.
He decided it was time to challenge Athaliah’s rule and reveal that Joash was alive and ready to be king. Alternate translation: [decided to act]

The phrase “commander of hundreds” is probably an official title for a military officer. This could mean: (1) the word “hundreds” represents the exact amount of soldiers that these commanders led. Alternate translation: [the commanders of 100 soldiers] or (2) the word translated as [hundreds] does not represent an exact number, but is the name of a military division. Alternate translation: [the commanders of military divisions]
These five men were the commanders of hundreds of soldiers.

2.q: the heads of the ancestral houses of Israel
2.note: Here “heads” is a metaphor for the most important part. And “houses” represents the families. Alternate translation: [leaders of the founding families of Israel] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

3.note: Here, “king” refers to Joash’s father. Alternate translation: [Joash, the son of the king]

4.q: will be guards at the doors
4.note: Alternate translation: [will be guards at the temple doors]

5.note: This gate may have also been called the “Middle Gate” or the “Sur Gate.” It was apparently an inner gate that was near the king’s palace.
This is a generalization that refers to all the people who are present. Alternate translation: [All the other people who are present]

6.q: Allow no one to come into the house of Yahweh
6.note: Alternate translation: [Do not allow anyone to come into the house of Yahweh]

6.q: But all the other people must obey the commands of Yahweh
6.note: It may be helpful to state that command. Alternate translation: [All the others must remain in the courtyard, obeying what Yahweh has commanded]

7.q: The Levites must surround the king on all sides
7.note: Alternate translation: [The Levites must surround the king on all sides in order to protect him]

7.q: all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand
7.note: Alternate translation: [all sides, and every temple guard should have his weapons and be ready to fight]

7.q: Whoever comes into the house, let him be killed
7.note: This did not include the temple guards and the priests. This can be stated explicitly and in active form. Alternate translation: [You must kill anyone except the temple guards and the priests who come into the temple] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

7.q: when he comes in and when he goes out
7.note: This could mean: (1) “at all times” or (2) “wherever he goes.”

8.note: This is a generalization to refer to all the people of Judah who were present in the courtyard that day.

8.q: served in every way in the manner in which Jehoiada the priest commanded
8.note: Alternate translation: [did exactly what Jehoiada the priest commanded] or [obeyed everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded]

8.q: Each one took his men … any of their divisions
8.note: The priests and guards served in divisions, with each group working for two weeks. This refers to the point in time when two divisions were present—the one ending their service and the one starting their service. Thus there were twice as many men as usual.

8.q: were to leave off serving on the Sabbath
8.note: Alternate translation: [were finishing their work on that Sabbath day]

10.note:
# General Information:

Throughout chapter 23, Joash is referred to as “the king.” It may be helpful to your readers to occasionally add “King Joash” or “Joash the king” to make his identity explicit.

10.q: with his weapon in his hand
10.note: This means they were ready to fight. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 23:7.

11.note: Here “king” refers to Joash’s father. Alternate translation: [Joash, the son of the king]
This is a symbolic act to show that they are making him king.

The symbolic act of giving him a scroll with the decrees shows that they expect him to obey them. It is unclear if these decrees were a portion of the law of Moses, or a separate set of rules for kings to obey. Alternate translation: [presented to him the covenant decrees that he should obey]
This was a symbolic act to show that he was chosen by God to be the king.
Alternate translation: [May the king live a long life]

13.note: This alerts the reader that the following information is very important.

13.q: standing by his pillar at the entrance
13.note: The relationship between the king and this particular pillar at the temple entrance is unclear.

13.q: All the people of the land
13.note: This is a generalization to show that many people participated in the event. Alternate translation: [A very large number of the people of the land]
This was a symbolic action to show her great distress.

Treason is acting to overthrow the government. Athaliah had killed the legitimate heirs of the king and made herself ruler in 2 Chronicles 22:10. She was angry that Joash became king in her place. The exclamation is repeated for emphasis. Alternate translation: [You are committing treason!]

14.note: Translate this man’s name as in 2 Chronicles 22:11.

The phrase “commander of hundreds” is probably an official title for a military officer. This could mean: (1) the word “hundreds” represents the exact amount of soldiers that these commanders led. Alternate translation: [the commanders of 100 soldiers] or (2) the word translated as [hundreds] does not represent an exact number, but is the name of a military division. See how you translated this in [2 Chronicles 23:1](ta:23). Alternate translation: [the commanders of military divisions]
Alternate translation: [who were leaders in the army]

14.q: Bring her out between the ranks
14.note: This could mean: (1) “Surround her and bring her out of the temple courtyard” or (2) “Remove her from the people in the temple courtyard”

14.q: anyone who follows her, let him be killed with the sword
14.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. It is implied that people who followed her would be trying to help her. Alternate translation: [Use your sword to kill anyone who comes to help her] (See also: [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))
Alternate translation: [For Jehoiada the priest had said]

15.q: as she went into the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king’s house
15.note: Some versions have “and took her to the Horse Gate near the entrance of the kings’ house”

16.note:
# General Information:

Throughout chapter 23, Joash is referred to as “the king.” It may be helpful to your readers to occasionally add “King Joash” or “Joash the king” to make his identity explicit.

17.q: all the people went to the house of Baal
17.note: This is a generalization that means a large group of the people did this. Alternate translation: [a very large group of the people went to the temple of Baal]
This is the name of a man.

18.q: under the hand of the priests
18.note: Here “hand” represents control. Alternate translation: [under the direction of the priests]

19.q: so that no one that was unclean in any way should enter
19.note: A person who is not acceptable for God’s purposes is spoken of as if they were physically unclean. Alternate translation: [so that no one that was unacceptable to God in any way should enter]

19.q: so that no one that was unclean in any way should enter
19.note: This can be stated in positive form. Alternate translation: [to make sure that only those who are clean could enter] or [to make sure only those who are acceptable to God could enter]

20.note: The phrase “commander of hundreds” is probably an official title for a military officer. This could mean: (1) the word “hundreds” represents the exact amount of soldiers that these commanders led. Alternate translation: [the commanders of 100 soldiers] or (2) the word translated as [hundreds] does not represent an exact number, but is the name of a military division. Alternate translation: [the commanders of military divisions] See how you translated this in [2 Chronicles 23:1](ta:23).

20.q: all the people of the land
20.note: This is a generalization that means he took very many people with him. Alternate translation: [a very large group of the people of Israel]

20.q: He brought down the king from the house of Yahweh
20.note: The temple was built on the highest hill in Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [He brought the king down from the temple to the palace]

21.q: So all the people of the land
21.note: This is generalization to say that most of the people rejoiced.
Here “the city” represents the people of the city, and “quiet” represents peace, since no one opposed Joash after Athaliah died. Alternate translation: [the people of the city were at peace]
